 GTA 6 developer says 'you can have your life in the game' as Rockstar outlines roleplay depth
 Rockstar's Aaron Garbut says GTA 6 players can buy beer, ride trains, or go clubbing in Leonida, saying 'you can have your life in the game.'
 VIEW GALLERY - 2 A poolside moment in GTA 6 reflects Rockstar's focus on letting players spend time in Leonida outside of missions. Jak Connor Tech and Science Editor Published Oct 29, 2026 12:37 PM CDT 45-second read time What you need to know
 GTA 6 lets players shape their time in Leonida through activities such as shopping, riding trains, clubbing, and spending time with Jason or Lucia. Rockstar says the game supports different play styles, though its roleplay possibilities have limits.

Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 will let players step away from crime and simply live in Leonida, with one of the game's leads telling a magazine that " you can have your life in the game. "
 2 A Grand Theft Auto 6 scene shows two men riding in an SUV, one of the many ways players can travel through Leonida outside of missions. VIEW GALLERY - 2 IMAGES Aaron Garbut, co-studio head and head of development at Rockstar North, told Edge , " You can really make the game what you want it to be at the time. " Garbut continued, " Whether that's more of a roleplay experience where you're buying cigarettes and beer in the shop and going on the train for the day, or going to a club. You can have your life in the game. " Rob Nelson, Rockstar North's other co-studio head, added that " it's more about trying to let people lean into the way they want to play. "

Jason and Lucia's relationship also gives players things to do outside of missions, as Edge explains their closeness is tracked on a four-point scale that rises through activities like walks on the beach, cycling, working out at the gym, or just driving around together.

 From TweakTown's coverage of this story.
 What gameplay effects are tied to Jason and Lucia's four-point relationship scale in GTA 6?
 Jason and Lucia's closeness rises on a four-point scale when they spend time together walking on the beach, cycling, working out, or driving around. No specific gameplay effects tied to reaching a particular point on the scale are identified. How does GTA 6's everyday roleplay fit alongside Jason and Lucia's story missions?
 GTA 6 lets players step away from Jason and Lucia's missions to spend a day in Leonida buying beer, riding transit, or going to a club. Time together outside missions also matters: walks, cycling, gym visits, and drives can raise their closeness on a four-point scale, though the roleplay possibilities have limits. What limits has Rockstar described for roleplaying in GTA 6?
 Rockstar has not described specific limits on GTA 6 roleplaying here. Its developers say players can choose everyday activities such as shopping, taking public transport, and going to clubs, while Edge writer Simon Parkin observes that these options operate within a "relatively narrow band of possibility." Can players choose whether Jason or Lucia takes part in GTA 6's everyday activities?
 GTA 6 includes everyday activities such as shopping, riding public transport, and going to clubs. Jason and Lucia can also do activities together, but the story does not say whether players can choose which of them takes part in a given activity. Got another question? Ask TweakBot.

Edge writer Simon Parkin points out that GTA 6's roleplay elements, while consequential, " operate within a relatively narrow band of possibility, " so there are limits to how far players can take it. Even so, it's a promising sign for the GTA roleplay community, which has spent years building this kind of experience in GTA 5 through mods and dedicated servers. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
